title: UK actors to get pay and consent rights over AI replicas under Equity deal
excerpt: A new Equity deal with producers would give UK actors pay and consent rights over AI digital replicas, but no explicit AI training protections.
content_html:
UK actors would be paid and asked for consent when their AI digital copies are used. That is the core of a new deal between the union Equity and producers’ body Pact, the Guardian reported. Equity’s leaders are urging its 8,000 members to approve it.

Producers would only get consent for one specific project, not for any use. Actors must also approve digital changes to scenes with agreed nudity or simulated sex.

Producers could not use a replica during a strike where consent is needed. They must also limit who can see replicas and take care to keep them safe.

But Equity said the deal does not clearly stop actors’ work being used to train AI.

The three-year deal also raises pay rates by 24% for major films and 9% for TV, according to the Guardian. Equity recommended the offer to members on Monday.

It follows a December ballot in which 99% of voting members backed refusing on-set body scans until stronger AI protections were agreed. In the US, the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA ratified its own deal with AI rules in June.

“We’ve achieved the best AI provisions in the business,” said Paul W Fleming, Equity’s general secretary.
